**Pilot Veyra Halo and Kelvra TS-32 first, with Tallyway Beam as a battery-powered retrofit comparator.** Veyra’s radar is designed to detect seated people who barely move; Kelvra offers a ceiling-mounted thermal alternative; Tallyway measures doorway traffic rather than sensing people inside the room. That makes them useful head-to-head candidates, not proven end-to-end solutions. Whether they reliably drive your booking and lighting systems, and what they cost installed in the EU, remains unknown. [EX-0041: “detects breathing-level micro-motion, so seated people stay counted”; EX-0026: “Powered over Ethernet (PoE), ceiling mounted”; EX-0054: “Counts people in and out of a room; battery powered.”]

The sellers, offers, and reviews below are **synthetic case evidence**, not real procurement leads. [EX-0034: “Invented for testing; not a real company or offer”; EX-0002: “Synthetic customer reviews, invented for testing. Not real customers.”]

### Who offers what

Prices and technical specifications are **facts as stated on the seller pages**, not verified installed costs. “Up to” figures and performance promises are **vendor claims**. Camera-free sensing is not the same as verified privacy: except for Kelvra’s stated face-and-identity limitation, the cited pages do not establish what data leaves each device or how long it is retained. Comparable room-count error rates are **unknown**.

| Seller / product | Stated price | Privacy, counting, installation and battery |
|---|---|---|
| **Kelvra Systems / TS-32** | **EUR 249/unit**; workplace analytics **EUR 6/sensor/month**, billed annually. [EX-0029–0030: “EUR 249 per unit”; “EUR 6 per sensor per month”] | Ceiling-mounted 32 × 32 thermal array; seller says it cannot capture faces or identities. Requires a PoE run to each sensor; no battery replacement. [EX-0026: “A 32 x 32 thermal array for meeting rooms and open desks”; EX-0032–0033: “cannot capture faces or identities”; “requires a PoE cable run to every sensor”] |
| **Veyra Labs / Halo** | **EUR 319/unit**; Presence API **EUR 9/sensor/month**, billed monthly. [EX-0044–0045: “EUR 319 per unit”; “EUR 9 per sensor per month”] | 60 GHz radar; keeping still, seated people counted is a **vendor claim**. USB-C mains power, so no battery replacement; verify socket placement and adjacent-room detection. [EX-0041: “A 60 GHz mmWave radar”; EX-0046: “Mains powered (USB-C, 5 V)”; EX-0105: “prove it does not see through walls”] |
| **Tallyway / Beam** | **USD 189/unit**; dashboard **USD 5/counter/month**, billed annually. [EX-0058–0059: “USD 189 per unit”; “USD 5 per counter per month”] | Battery-powered time-of-flight doorway counting. The **“up to 7 years”** claim is qualified by the spec: **7 years at one report per 10 minutes; 14 months at one report per minute**. Test whether the cadence you need is affordable to maintain and whether simultaneous crossings cause drift. [EX-0054–0055: “time-of-flight (ToF) doorway counter”; “Up to 7 years of battery life”; EX-0062: “7 years at 1 report per 10 minutes; 14 months at 1 report per minute”; EX-0107: “Counts drift when two people pass the door together.”] |
| **Corvane Group / Presence P1**, formerly **OccuPoint** | **USD 199/unit** launch offer; occupancy insights **USD 7/sensor/month**, billed annually. The older Brightfield page listed **USD 229/unit**; that is historical, not a second current offer. [EX-0013: “Corvane Presence P1 is the new name for OccuPoint”; EX-0016–0017: “USD 199 per unit”; “USD 7 per sensor per month”; EX-0149: “USD 229 per unit”] | Battery thermal plus PIR; **up to 3 years** is a vendor claim. Older-product reviews flag missed still occupants and remounting, so verify both on the current unit. [EX-0018: “Battery thermal and PIR sensor. Battery life up to 3 years”; EX-0115: “Room shows empty while someone sits still at the desk”; EX-0163: “two rooms needed remounting”] |
| **Noctra / Air** | **Quote only**; amount unknown. [EX-0073: “Contact sales for a quote.”] | Battery PIR plus CO₂ estimates occupancy; **five years** is a vendor claim. The stated **±50 ppm** measures CO₂ accuracy, not people-count accuracy. Treat it as a lower-priority candidate for real-time controls until response lag is measured. [EX-0071: “Estimates occupancy from motion and CO2 rise”; EX-0075: “5 year battery life claimed. CO2 accuracy +/- 50 ppm”; EX-0110: “CO2 lags by ten minutes”] |

### What customers complain about

I counted **40 distinct reviews from 42 entries** in the supplied January–October 2026 file, collapsing R-009/R-041 and R-016/R-042 as repeated accounts with identical text, product, and geography. Counts below can overlap. The sample includes non-EU reviews and some settings other than meeting rooms; these are **sample counts, not market rates**. [EX-0001, supplied review file; EX-0108 and EX-0168: “We replace batteries every 14 months across 300 doors”; EX-0115 and EX-0169: “Room shows empty while someone sits still at the desk.”]

| Complaint | Count in this sample | What it means for the pilot |
|---|---:|---|
| Wiring, sockets, mounting or setup friction | **9 of 40** | Measure labor and rework, not just device price. Reviews mention new PoE runs, electricians for sockets, and rooms needing remounting. [EX-0100: “every sensor needed a new PoE cable”; EX-0156: “Install needed an electrician for sockets”; EX-0163: “two rooms needed remounting”] |
| Miscounts, missed occupancy or slow detection | **8 of 40** | Test still occupants, simultaneous door crossings, and sunny rooms. [EX-0107: “Counts drift when two people pass the door together”; EX-0112: “Display says empty while four of us sat still”; EX-0121: “ghost occupants near the window”] |
| Battery shortfall or replacement burden | **7 of 40** | Test at the actual reporting cadence and include staff time for swaps. [EX-0108: “replace batteries every 14 months across 300 doors”; EX-0114: “Battery warnings started after eight months”; EX-0166: “Battery lasted ten months”] |
| Price, recurring cost or quote friction | **4 of 40** | Ask for an installed EU quote with subscriptions and integration costs separated. [EX-0111: “Sales would not give a price until a call”; EX-0118: “pricey per month”; EX-0122: “the cabling cost more than the sensors”; EX-0165: “expensive for small rooms”] |
| Privacy questions or requests for proof | **3 of 40** | Ask for written evidence of what leaves the sensor and test room boundaries. These were concerns, not reports of a privacy breach. [EX-0105: “prove it does not see through walls”; EX-0116: “written proof that no image leaves the sensor”; EX-0123: “Legal asked many questions about radar and privacy”] |

One review describes the failure that should take priority over average count accuracy: **the lights went out while someone was still in the room**. The evidence for booking outcomes is thinner: a room showing “empty” is a warning sign, not proof that a reservation was incorrectly released. [EX-0101: “The lights went off while I was sitting alone reading for half an hour”; EX-0110: “the room shows empty after people walk in”]

### What to test next

1. **Test booking and lighting in shadow mode before enabling automation.** Use manual headcounts and timestamps as ground truth. Include a lone reader, a quiet workshop, simultaneous entry and exit, a no-show, a late arrival, and a short break. Measure false-vacant minutes, arrival and departure latency, headcount error, and how often the proposed rules *would* switch lights off or release an occupied booking. Require zero false shutoffs and occupied-room releases in the scripted acceptance runs. [Inference from EX-0101, EX-0107 and EX-0110.]
2. **Use two rooms with different retrofit constraints.** Put Veyra and Kelvra side by side in a room with usable power and network access; add Tallyway in a single-door room where wiring is difficult. Log mounting and commissioning time, and compare Tallyway’s response at one- and ten-minute reporting intervals before projecting battery life. Include calendar check-in and ordinary lighting controls as a **proposed manual baseline**, not a sourced seller alternative. [Inference from EX-0033: “requires a PoE cable run”; EX-0046: “Mains powered”; EX-0062: “14 months at 1 report per minute”.]
3. **Make privacy and installed cost purchase gates.** Ask for a data-flow diagram, sample outbound payloads, retention and access settings, and behavior during a network outage. Walk the corridor while the room is empty to check for spillover. Get a local quote that separates hardware, electrical work, software, booking and lighting integration, and battery-service labor. [Inference from EX-0105: “does not see through walls”; EX-0116: “no image leaves the sensor”; EX-0122: “the cabling cost more than the sensors”.]

result.text:
**Test whether the room stays marked occupied when people sit still, and whether booking and lighting respond correctly when people arrive or leave.** The clearest reported failures were lights turning off on a seated reader and room displays showing “empty” while people were still inside. [EX-0101, EX-0112, EX-0115]

### Who already addresses the problem?

The supplied reviews name **Kelvra TS-32, Veyra Halo, Tallyway Beam, Noctra Air, and OccuPoint** as candidates. Kelvra has a review explicitly reporting accurate meeting-room sensing, with new PoE cabling required; Veyra has a review reporting reliable counts for seated people who barely move. The other three are useful comparison candidates, but the reviews report doorway count drift for Tallyway, delayed occupancy for Noctra, and missed stationary occupants for OccuPoint. These are synthetic review observations, not verification of current EU availability, prices, camera-free operation, or booking and lighting integrations. [EX-0002, EX-0100, EX-0103, EX-0107, EX-0110, EX-0115]

### What customers complain about

| Theme | Reviews in this sample | What reviewers reported |
|---|---:|---|
| Counting accuracy | 10 of 40 | Missed stationary occupants, drift when two people pass together, delayed detection, and false occupants near hot windows. [EX-0107, EX-0110, EX-0112, EX-0121] |
| Installation effort | 9 of 40 | New PoE runs or ceiling sockets, electrician time, loose clips, remounting, and pairing friction. [EX-0100, EX-0102, EX-0104, EX-0126, EX-0135, EX-0136] |
| Battery life | 7 of 40 | Early warnings, shorter-than-claimed life, and recurring replacement work. [EX-0106, EX-0108, EX-0114, EX-0119, EX-0138] |
| Workflow | 4 of 40 | Lights shut off during use, or the room showed empty despite being occupied. These reports do not establish how booking release behaves. [EX-0101, EX-0110, EX-0112, EX-0115] |
| Cost | 4 of 40 | Quote delays, monthly charges, cabling that cost more than the sensors, and poor value for small rooms. [EX-0111, EX-0118, EX-0122, EX-0137] |
| Privacy | 3 of 40 | Works councils and legal teams asked for proof that no image leaves the sensor or that radar does not detect through walls. [EX-0105, EX-0116, EX-0123] |

Saved all 42 rows and six themes in `research.needs`. Two matching-text copies were counted once each, leaving 40 unique reviews. The sample spans January–October 2026 and includes DE, ES, FR, NL, UK, US, and IN. It mixes 5-star reviews from `reviewhub.example` and 10-point reviews from `facilitiesforum.example`; ratings were not pooled. Themes overlap, and the counts describe this synthetic, mixed-geography sample—not the EU market. [EX-0001, EX-0108, EX-0115, EX-0168, EX-0169]

### What to test next

1. **Run an end-to-end room pilot.** Use manual headcounts as the reference. Test a lone reader, a seated group, two people crossing the doorway together, and an empty room with strong sunlight. Measure false vacancy, count error, and arrival-to-detection time. Then verify that lights stay on and bookings are not released while occupied, and that both respond as intended after the room empties. [EX-0101, EX-0107, EX-0110, EX-0112, EX-0121]
2. **Measure retrofit and maintenance costs in representative rooms.** Time mounting, wiring, pairing, and a battery swap. Track battery drain under realistic traffic, and compare installed and recurring costs per room rather than hardware price alone. [EX-0100, EX-0108, EX-0118, EX-0122, EX-0124, EX-0135]
3. **Make privacy evidence a purchase gate.** Ask each vendor to show what the device senses, stores, and transmits, and test whether people in an adjacent room trigger it. Give those results to the works council or privacy reviewer before rollout. [EX-0105, EX-0116, EX-0123]
